speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. To better understand your condition, can you tell me if your arm pain radiates in a specific pattern, such as down your thumb or pinky finger?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has your neck or arm pain worsened significantly since the motor vehicle accident three years ago, or is it strictly related to the diabetes and hypertension you've been managing?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS).

The combination of progressive weakness, fasciculations, and absent reflexes alongside sensory symptoms is highly suggestive of ALS. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI to rule out compressive myelopathy, though the clinical picture strongly favors a motor neuron disease.
